summary: FIX#4 visfAtlas retest after switching to vol.setColormapLabel(layerCfg.colormapLabel). PRIMARY CRITERION PASSES: multi-hue categorical rendering is now visibly correct — yellow / green / blue / red / magenta ROIs are clearly distinguishable across the occipital/temporal cortex in the axial slice and on the 3D render. The colormapLabel API is the right pathway. SECONDARY CRITERIA: colormap-visfAtlas dropdown now shows 'visfAtlas' as both selected value AND as a real <option> entry (LayerControl COLORMAPS list updated). HOWEVER two regressions remain that block the spec's third sub-criterion: (a) [data-testid=crosshair-labels] never appears because loadAtlasLabels() in Dashboard.jsx throws 'data is not iterable' — the visfAtlas_labels.json file is keyed as {"1":"name",...} (a dict) but the parser does `for (const it of data) tbl[it.index] = it.name`, which only handles array-of-objects. (b) [data-testid=crosshair-val-visfAtlas] reads '0' at almost every colored ROI click (one click returned '53.72', which is a floating-point value impossible for an integer 1..33 label volume — suggesting the visfAtlas-labelled overlay's data.values entry is either reporting from the wrong volume or the volume name in niivue's onLocationChange callback does not match what our shortLayerName() lookup uses, causing a testid mismatch).

ui_bugs.issue: Parser expects labels JSON to be an array of {index,name} objects, but /atlases/visfAtlas_labels.json is a dict {"1":"lh_mFus_faces","2":"lh_pFus_faces",...,"33":"rh_v3v_retinotopic"}. Result: TypeError 'data is not iterable' thrown on every visfAtlas toggle, atlasLabelsRef.current['visfAtlas'] is never populated, so the if-branch in handleLocationChange that would set labels[shortAtlas(v.name)] never fires, and [data-testid=crosshair-labels] is never rendered for visfAtlas. Fix: detect dict vs array shape in loadAtlasLabels — `if (Array.isArray(data)) ... else if (typeof data === 'object') for (const [k,v] of Object.entries(data)) tbl[parseInt(k,10)] = v;`

[data-testid=crosshair-val-visfAtlas] reads '0' at 4/5 visibly-colored ROI clicks (occipital green/blue/yellow patches in axial), and once read '53.72' which is impossible for an integer label volume (1..33). 53.72 matches the MNI152 base-volume intensity at that voxel, suggesting volume-name confusion or that the visfAtlas volume's `name` in niivue's onLocationChange data.values is not 'visfAtlas' (perhaps it's the URL basename 'visfAtlas_maxprob' or similar), so the row built by `valueRows.push({ name: shortLayerName(v.name), value: v.value })` gets a different name than the test expects. Also possible: the overlay volume is loaded but its `img[]` typed array contains floats not ints at the queried voxel (rare for label volumes, but worth checking). Recommend logging `data.values.map(v=>v.name+'='+v.value)` once in handleLocationChange to confirm the actual layer key used.

Console emits 'niivue-warn padding colormap: indices expected end with 255 not 34' multiple times when setColormapLabel is called with the 34-entry VISFATLAS_COLORMAP whose I array ends at 34. Cosmetic — rendering works — but suggests the I/indices array in VISFATLAS_COLORMAP should be normalised so its last entry is 255 (not 34) per niivue's preferred convention. Niivue is auto-padding which is what makes it work, but the warning is noisy.

integration_issues.issue: Categorical render is correct; the value-at-crosshair pathway is broken in two distinct ways: (1) labels JSON parser bug — visfAtlas_labels.json dict not recognised; (2) layer-name mismatch (or alignment) causing val readout to be 0 at clicked colored voxels. Both must be fixed for the spec's third sub-criterion (label name + non-zero int 1..33 in crosshair).

action_items: Fix loadAtlasLabels in /app/frontend/src/pages/Dashboard.jsx to accept dict-shaped labels JSON. Suggested patch: after `const data = await res.json();` add `if (Array.isArray(data)) { for (const it of data) tbl[it.index] = it.name; } else if (data && typeof data === 'object') { for (const [k,v] of Object.entries(data)) tbl[parseInt(k,10)] = v; }`. The visfAtlas_labels.json shipped under /atlases/ uses {"1":"lh_mFus_faces",...} dict form; AAL/HO/Destrieux use array form — both need to keep working.

Debug why [data-testid=crosshair-val-visfAtlas] is 0 at visibly colored ROI voxels. Likely causes (in order of probability): (1) niivue's onLocationChange data.values uses the volume's URL-derived name (e.g. 'visfAtlas_maxprob') NOT the .name we set, so the row testid becomes `crosshair-val-visfAtlas_ma…` (truncated by shortLayerName's 12-char rule) and a separate `crosshair-val-visfAtlas` either doesn't exist or matches an unrelated volume. Verify by logging `console.log(values.map(v=>v.name))` in handleLocationChange. (2) The overlay NIfTI's affine doesn't align with MNI152 — verify with FSL `fslinfo` that visfAtlas_maxprob.nii.gz has identical qform/sform to mni152.nii.gz.

Optional: normalise VISFATLAS_COLORMAP.I to end at 255 instead of 34 (e.g. spread I values linearly 0,8,16,…,255 over the 34 control points) to silence the 'padding colormap' niivue warning. Functional behavior is unchanged; rendering already works thanks to niivue's auto-pad.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/src/pages/Dashboard.jsx loadAtlasLabels (~line 181-192): silent try/catch swallows the 'data is not iterable' TypeError as console.warn — leaves atlasLabelsRef.current[id] undefined and produces a feature regression (no crosshair-labels) without UI feedback. Either (a) support both array and dict shapes, or (b) at minimum surface a toast.error so future regressions are noticed.

/app/frontend/src/components/NiivueViewer.jsx addOverlayFromUrl (~line 250-265): vol.name is set to layerCfg.id after addVolumeFromUrl returns. Verify whether niivue's onLocationChange callback's data.values[].name reflects this reassignment or the original URL-derived name. If the latter, either set the name BEFORE niivue caches it internally, or change the lookup in handleLocationChange to match by URL-suffix.

/app/frontend/src/lib/visfAtlasColormap.js (not viewed in this iteration but inferred from console warning): VISFATLAS_COLORMAP.I array ends with 34 instead of 255. Niivue prefers I[last]===255 — auto-padding is happening every render. Trivially fixable.

context_for_next_testing_agent: FIX#4 is HALF-DONE. The big rendering win is real: vol.setColormapLabel() produces the expected 33-ROI multi-hue display. Two follow-ups remain: (1) the labels JSON parser in Dashboard.loadAtlasLabels() must accept dict-shaped JSON (visfAtlas_labels.json is keyed '1'..'33' as strings, not array-of-objects). (2) crosshair-val-visfAtlas reads 0 at colored voxels — most likely volume-name mismatch (niivue's data.values entries probably carry the URL-basename 'visfAtlas_maxprob' not the assigned .name 'visfAtlas'); confirm by logging data.values in handleLocationChange. After both fixes the spec's third sub-criterion (label name + non-zero integer in crosshair) should pass.
rca of the issue: RCA — crosshair-labels never renders: Dashboard.loadAtlasLabels (lines ~181-192) does `const data = await res.json(); for (const it of data) tbl[it.index] = it.name;` — that for-of throws TypeError when `data` is a plain object dict. visfAtlas_labels.json is `{"1":"lh_mFus_faces",...,"33":"rh_v3v_retinotopic"}`. AAL / HO / Destrieux ship as `[{"index":1,"name":"…"}, …]` arrays, so the parser was never tested on a dict-shaped labels file. RCA — crosshair-val=0: visibly colored voxels return 0 in [data-testid=crosshair-val-visfAtlas]; meanwhile a different click returned 53.72 which is the MNI152 base intensity at that voxel — strongly indicating the testid is matching a row whose v.name is NOT 'visfAtlas'. Most likely niivue's onLocationChange data.values[].name reflects the URL-basename ('visfAtlas_maxprob') not the .name we reassign in addOverlayFromUrl. shortLayerName('visfAtlas_maxprob') yields 'visfAtlas_ma…' (truncated), producing a different testid than the test expects. Fix: either set vol.name BEFORE niivue caches its internal label, or update shortLayerName/handleLocationChange to canonicalise visfAtlas_* → 'visfAtlas'.
